**[Suggestion]** `cursor.repo` gains a permanent entry per project and is never pruned or bounded, while `saveCursor()` re-serializes the whole map synchronously once per todo.

`validateCursor` (lines 66-73) only type-checks the map — never its size or the shape of its values — and `PollingChannelBase.saveCursor()` is a blocking `mkdirSync` + `writeFileSync` + `renameSync` of the entire JSON blob. It is called on all three branches of this loop (lines 153, 160, 185), and `runLoop` calls it *again* right after `pollOnce()` returns, so a cycle with T todos performs T+1 write-rename sequences where the last is always redundant.

The keys are remotely influenced: `TodoLists.all()` returns todos from every project on the instance, and this write happens even when every note was rejected by the gate. Verified: 50 todos from 50 distinct projects produced 50 permanent entries; 300 projects produced ~17 KB. Cost per todo is O(projects ever seen), so write volume grows quadratically over the channel's lifetime.

The GitHub sibling bounds its analogous state explicitly — `MAX_DISPATCHED_BODIES = 500` with `list.slice(-MAX_DISPATCHED_BODIES)` (`GithubAdapter.ts:29,331-335`), commented "Bounded to the most recent entries so the cursor stays small."

Suggest: keep the N most recently touched keys on write, and drop `saveCursor()` from the two skip branches — the trailing `runLoop` save already covers a monotonic timestamp.

_— claude-opus-5[1m] via Qwen Code /qreview_

**[Suggestion]** When `protectPinnedMemory` is true and the path is NOT in pinned (the common case for Dream writes to ordinary memory files), `realpathExistingOrNew(filePath)` runs twice on the same file — once inside `isProtectedPinnedMemoryPath` and again inside `isAllowedMemoryPath`. — Failure scenario: a Dream consolidation session producing 50 write operations to ordinary memory paths executes 50 extra synchronous `realpathSync` calls, each blocking the event loop.

Suggested fix: resolve the candidate path once before calling either function and pass the pre-resolved path as an optional parameter.

_— qwen3.7-max via Qwen Code /review_

**[Suggestion]** `realpathExistingOrNew(literalPinnedRoot)` resolves the pinned root's real path inside the `.some()` loop, once per memory root, on every `write_file`/`edit` evaluation. The pinned root directories are stable for the session's lifetime but are re-resolved from disk each time. — Failure scenario: during a Dream session with 2 memory roots and 100 tool evaluations, `realpathSync` is called ~200 times on stable directory paths that don't change.

Suggested fix: compute the resolved pinned root once at config creation time (in `createMemoryScopedAgentConfig`) and store it in the closure, or memoize it per memory root.

`saveCursor()` performs three synchronous filesystem operations (`mkdirSync`, `writeFileSync`, `renameSync`) on every iteration of the todo loop. The base class `PollingChannelBase.runLoop()` already calls `saveCursor()` once after `pollOnce()` returns.

— Failure scenario: A poll returns 50 pending todos → 150 synchronous disk operations in the hot path, blocking the event loop.

**Quadratic backtracking here makes the documented 6500 ms internal wall-clock budget unenforceable.**

This regex runs over the **full, up-to-1 MiB** submitted prompt, before the 512-code-point truncation at line 124. `-` and `_` are inside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` but are not `\w`, so every hyphen/underscore in the input creates a fresh `\b` start position whose greedy star can span the rest of the string.

Measured through the real exported `createAutoRecallQuery` (tsx, Node 22, input `'a-'.repeat(n)`):

| prompt bytes | time |
| --- | --- |
| 20 KB | 1,143 ms |
| 50 KB | 7,316 ms |
| 100 KB | 29,571 ms |

At the `MAX_HOOK_INPUT_BYTES` cap that extrapolates to roughly 50 minutes of pinned CPU.

Because the work is synchronous, the `HOOK_WALL_CLOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` timer **cannot fire** — the event loop is blocked. So `docs/design/direct-external-context-auto-recall.md`'s "Hook internal wall-clock budget: 6500 milliseconds, which aborts the provider signal" does not hold across this window, and what actually terminates the process is Qwen's outer `killChild()` (`hookRunner.ts:623`) at the managed 8000 ms deadline. User-visible effect: the submission stalls the full 8 s before the model call while a child process pegs a core, then fails open.

Suggested fix: bound the sanitizer input before any regex runs — only 512 code points survive anyway, so slicing to a few KB up front costs nothing and caps the work. Optionally also drop `-`/`_` from the character class.

Realistic trigger is a plain **unfenced** paste of a base64url or long kebab/snake-case blob; fenced code is already stripped by the preceding step.

**This test gives false assurance — it doesn't exercise the backtracking shape it's named for.**

`'token'.repeat(200_000)` is one unbroken run of word characters, so `\b` in `ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN` matches only at offset 0. That's exactly **one** start position, hence the 3 ms result — the pathological case needs *many* `\b` positions, which requires non-word characters inside the run.

Changing the input to `'a-'.repeat(20_000)` (40 KB, well under the 1 MiB stdin cap) blows the 2000 ms assertion at ~1.1 s, and `'a-'.repeat(50_000)` takes 7.3 s. Please use that shape here so the guard actually regresses if the sanitizer's input bound is removed.

**[Suggestion]** Give unverified benchmarks a valid output path

This tells Agent 4 to flag a benchmark while also declaring its absence non-defective, but the shared agent contract exposes only actionable findings and explicitly excludes non-defects. For a hardware-specific latency claim, the agent must therefore either drop the caveat or manufacture a finding. Add a propagated observation channel, or make the outcome actionable by requesting the benchmark script, environment, and raw results; otherwise specify that an unreproducible claim produces no finding.

*— Codex GPT-5 via Qwen Code /review*
